medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: The Office of Student Affairs is charged to enforce college-wide policies and practices, including the Leave of Absence.  The Leave of Absence policy was written to address medical, personal and academic reasons for absence. All requests are considered on a case-by-case basis through the Student Progress Committee.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
The Tucson campus has an active student body engaged in the future of medicine, patient care and education by virtue of activism and professional development in any number of specialties.  Local, state-wide and national professional associations also provide students the opportunity to collaborate with practicing physicians, academicians and peers through speaking engagements, clinics and other endeavors.  Student Government is highly visible, accessible and serves as the collective voice for medical students.  Humanism and honor societies are also a part of the campus environment.
https://medicine.arizona.edu/internal-resources/student-affairs/student-life
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
The College of Medicine – Tucson’s clinical partner is Banner – University Medicine, a premier academic medical network that is part of Arizona-based Banner Health – one of the largest nonprofit health-care systems in the country. 
Faculty physicians give our medical students an up close and personal experience in health care in Banner’s two Tucson hospitals: Banner – University Medical Center Tucson and Banner – University Medical Center South. 
Since partnering with Banner in 2015, the College has been able to hire 200 new faculty members and invest in five new residency programs. In 2018 Banner Medical Group opened their brand new state-of-the art Banner University Medical Center-Tucson (9-story 649 bed  academic hospital) and Banner University Medical Center - Tucson North Campus. Students rotate at these sites, as well as other associated training sites within and outside of the BUMG.

medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The educational track utilizes a similar core structure, while each also offers distinct elements. The first eighteen months of curricula  are structured in integrated blocks that focus on organ systems. The Clerkship and Transition to Residency sections of the curriculum consist of required clinical clerkships in key disciplines and significant time for elective work. Basic and clinical science are interwoven with threads: behavioral science and humanism, health and society, and interprofessional education. Both curricula emphasize active learning, guided independent learning, working in teams, and early clinical experience. Nearly all students take part in our robust co-curricular activities, including medical student research, rural health and service learning programs.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: The Tucson campus offers curricular time to explore primary care interests.  Particularly, the Rural Health Professions Program is a college-wide effort to match medical students with physicians working in small towns throughout Arizona, providing a comprehensive rural experience throughout the four years of medical school. Building a diverse and inclusive community is the cornerstone of excellence and necessary to foster medical innovation.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
Medical Student Research Program: Our Medical Student Research Program (MSRP) enriches medical student education beyond classrooms and clerkships. Our student research fellows:

Explore the current horizens of basic and clinical biology
Develop research skills
Learn to communicate effectively
Learn to identify and solve problems systematically
Meet distinguished visiting physicians and scientists
Work closely with faculty and students in diverse laboratory and patient care settings

Research Distinction Track: The research distinction track offers students the opportunity to explore medical research while attending medical school. This track is designed to engage medical students at the forefront of scientific medicine and to engage in their own research interests. Students in this track will:

Critically review published medical literature
Design and implement an extensive research proposal
Author reports and publishable articles
Experience the scientific method as a process, not an a

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
The MD program at the College of Medicine – Tucson is designed to train highly skilled physicians dedicated to improving patient care and advancing the state of medical knowledge.

Students at the College of Medicine  – Tucson graduate with the skills to succeed in modern medicine. In addition to diagnosing, treating and preventing disease, our students:

Solve problems
Work with patients
Pose and pursue research questions
Follow the latest scientific literature
Apply new knowledge to practice
Participate in professional discourse
Engage with the social, ethical and economic challenges facing modern health care

The Tucson campus of UA enrolled its first class of medical students in 1967 and is located adjacent to the main UA campus. We are dedicated to enrolling students who are interested in both their professional and their personal growth, who not only are academically fit, but who also demonstrate a commitment to medicine and its constant evolution.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The College of Medicine – Tucson trains future physicians to provide high-quality and compassionate care, develops scientists focused on exciting discoveries, and nurtures undergraduate and graduate students interested the many professions in health care and the health sciences.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout:
The APME program offers a unique educational experience for talented students anticipating a career in medicine or medical science. The APME fosters flexibility and creativity in undergraduate education while reducing the pressures related to gaining acceptance to medical school. Students are encouraged to take advantage of the reduced pressure by exploring and challenging themselves personally and professionally to prepare a solid foundation for success in medical school and for leadership roles in their careers in medicine.

Students apply to APME once they have entered their senior year of high school and have been accepted at the University of Arizona. A limited number of students are accepted each year to the program.

The APME program will take a minimum of seven years to complete, three years of undergraduate studies, and four years to complete an MD degree. Students will be required to complete a sequence of required premedical courses during their undergraduate coursework.

medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
All University of Arizona College of Medicine – Tucson (COM-T) undergraduate medical students must meet the Technical Standards throughout their enrollment in the MD Program. Satisfaction of the Technical Standards is an ongoing academic requirement.
Technical Standards Evaluations are used to determine if a student’s academic or behavioral performance is or may be affected by impairment that includes, but is not limited to, medical, behavioral, or substance abuse issues.
The purpose of a Technical Standards Evaluation is to determine the student’s ability to perform their academic and clinical duties responsibly and safely, meaning that the student is not a danger to patients, colleagues, self, or anyone in the learning environment or on University or clinical properties.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
1)The Pathway to Medicine Postbaccalaureate Program is tailored towards career-changers and students who have already earned a bachelor’s degree but are missing pre-reqs needed for admission to medical school. PMPP allows students to complete undergraduate courses that fulfill pre-reqs for the University of Arizona COM - Tucson and other US medical schools, while also providing structured mentorship, application development, and access to medical school resources and support.

2)The Pre-Medical Admissions Pathway (P-MAP) Program is a 13-month, full-time, intensive medical school preparation program designed to prepare Arizona students to succeed in the rigors of medical school. The program includes coursework toward a Master of Science degree in cellular and molecular medicine, professional and clinical development, success seminars, and conditional admission to the College of Medicine – Tucson MD program.
For informaion contact Auralia Walls, abw2@arizona.edu.

medSchoolMdPathway.programDesc:
The Primary Care Accelerated Medical Pathway (PCAMP) is designed to tackle the primary care physician shortage and reduce student debt by providing a streamlined route into the family medicine residency program at the University of Arizona College of Medicine – Tucson.
PCAMP is an 3+3+3 accelerated medical school program that includes:
3 years of medical school
•	3 years of residency training with the UA COM – Tucson Family Medicine Program
•	3 years as a faculty member at the COM – Tucson
medSchoolMdPathway.eligibleApplicants: Applicants that have been invited to participate in Multiple Mini Interviews with the University of Arizona College of Medicine – Tucson are able to apply to  3 Year MD PCAMP..
medSchoolMdPathway.applicationProcess: Post interview an additional application tab in the AMP application portal allows applicants to fill out the PCAMP application. Selected applicants will complete additional virtual interviews with the Family Medicine Residency Program.
medSchoolMdPathway.residencyAffiliationPathway: Directed residency option for all Three-Year MD students
